name: LAMA3
summary: LAMA3, junctional epidermolysis bullosa type 2 (JEB2), the form found in the American Saddlebred and related breeds - a recessive lethal. A deletion of 6,589 base pairs spanning exons 24 to 27 leaves no working alpha-3 chain of laminin-332, the protein that anchors the outer skin to the layer beneath. A random sample of American Saddlebred foals born in 2007 found 9 carriers in 175, about 5 percent. A different gene from the draft breeds' LAMC2 form (JEB1).

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: LAMA3 carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy of jeb. The horse is completely normal and there is no way to see it - but half its foals inherit the copy, and two carriers bred together are the only way junctional epidermolysis bullosa (lama3) appears.

phenotypes.name: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa (LAMA3)
phenotypes.description: The layer that anchors the outer skin to the body does not hold. The skin and the lining of the mouth blister and come away, and the hoof wall may detach so that the hooves slough. The foal does not survive.
